docs.title: Welcome to the DevOps Master Guide
docs.text: This guide is designed to help you master DevOps tools and practices, starting from the absolute basics. Whether you are on Windows, macOS, or Linux, we have you covered.

docs.title: What's Inside?
docs.text:
• Learning Path: A step-by-step roadmap to becoming a DevOps Engineer.
  • Installation Guides: Detailed instructions to set up your environment on any OS.
  • Tools & Commands: Scenario-based cheat sheets and guides for essential tools like Git, Docker, Kubernetes, and more.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: If you are new to DevOps, start with the Learning Path to understand the journey ahead. Then, visit the Installation Guides to prepare your computer.

docs.title: DevOps Learning Path
docs.text: Follow this roadmap to build your skills step-by-step.

docs.title: Phase 1: Prerequisites & OS Concepts
docs.text:
• Understand Linux Basics (File system, Permissions, Shell Scripting)
  • Networking Fundamentals (DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, Firewalls)
  • Goal: Be comfortable using the terminal.

docs.title: Phase 2: Version Control
docs.text:
• Git: Learn to track changes, branch, and merge.
  • GitHub/GitLab: Collaborate with others.
  • Goal: Contribute to a repository.

docs.title: Phase 3: Containerization
docs.text:
• Docker: Learn to package applications.
  • Understand Images, Containers, and Dockerfiles.
  • Goal: Containerize a simple web application.

docs.title: Phase 4: CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Deployment)
docs.text:
• Jenkins or GitHub Actions.
  • Automate testing and deployment.
  • Goal: Build a pipeline that deploys your app automatically.

docs.title: Phase 5: Cloud Providers
docs.text:
• AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
  • Learn EC2, S3, IAM, VPC.
  • Goal: Deploy your app to the cloud manually.

docs.title: Phase 6: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
docs.text:
• Terraform: Provision infrastructure using code.
  • Ansible: Configuration management.
  • Goal: Automate the creation of your cloud resources.

docs.title: Phase 7: Container Orchestration
docs.text:
• Kubernetes: Manage containerized applications at scale.
  • Pods, Services, Deployments.
  • Goal: Deploy your app to a Kubernetes cluster.

docs.title: Phase 8: Monitoring & Observability
docs.text:
• Prometheus & Grafana.
  • ELK Stack.
  • Goal: Monitor your application's health and logs.

docs.title: Installation Guides
docs.text:
Choose your operating system to get started with setting up your DevOps environment.

  • Windows 11
  • macOS
  • Linux

docs.title: Linux DevOps Setup
docs.text: This guide assumes you are using a Debian-based distribution (like Ubuntu).

docs.title: 1. Update System
docs.text:
Always start by updating your package list.

sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

docs.title: 2. Install Git
docs.text:
sudo apt install git -y
git --version

docs.title: 3. Install VS Code
docs.text:
1. Download the .deb package from the VS Code website.
  2. Install it using apt:
sudo apt install ./<file-name>.deb

Alternatively, use Snap:

sudo snap install code --classic

docs.title: 4. Install Docker
docs.text:
Install Docker Engine using the convenience script (for development environments):

curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com -o get-docker.sh
sudo sh get-docker.sh

Add your user to the docker group to run without sudo:

sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
# Log out and log back in for changes to take effect

docs.title: 5. Install Additional Tools
docs.text:
# Install curl and wget if missing
sudo apt install curl wget -y

docs.title: macOS DevOps Setup
docs.text: This guide covers setting up a DevOps environment on macOS using Homebrew.

docs.title: 1. Install Homebrew
docs.text:
Homebrew is the package manager for macOS. Open Terminal and run:

/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

Follow the on-screen instructions to add Homebrew to your PATH.

docs.title: 2. Install iTerm2 (Optional but Recommended)
docs.text:
iTerm2 is a replacement for the default Terminal app.

brew install --cask iterm2

docs.title: 3. Install Core Tools
docs.text:
Install Git and other essentials:

brew install git wget curl tree

docs.title: 4. Install VS Code
docs.text:
brew install --cask visual-studio-code

Recommended Extensions: * Docker * HashiCorp Terraform * YAML * Kubernetes

docs.title: 5. Install Docker
docs.text:
We recommend using Docker Desktop for Mac.

brew install --cask docker

Start Docker from your Applications folder.

docs.title: 6. Verify Installation
docs.text:
Open a new terminal window and run:

git --version
docker --version

docs.title: Windows 11 DevOps Setup
docs.text: This guide will help you set up a robust DevOps environment on Windows 11 using WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux). This allows you to run Linux tools natively on Windows.

docs.title: 1. Install WSL2
docs.text:
Open PowerShell as Administrator and run:

wsl --install

Restart your computer when prompted. By default, this installs Ubuntu.

docs.title: 2. Install Windows Terminal
docs.text: Download Windows Terminal from the Microsoft Store. It provides a better experience for managing multiple shells (PowerShell, WSL, Command Prompt).

docs.title: 3. Install VS Code
docs.text:
Download and install Visual Studio Code.

Extensions to install: * WSL: To edit files inside your Linux distro. * Docker: For managing containers. * HashiCorp Terraform: For Infrastructure as Code. * YAML: For editing configuration files.

docs.title: 4. Install Docker Desktop
docs.text:
1. Download Docker Desktop for Windows.
  2. Run the installer and ensure "Use WSL 2 based engine" is checked.
  3. Start Docker Desktop.
  4. Go to Settings > Resources > WSL Integration and enable integration with your Ubuntu distro.

docs.title: 5. Verify Installation
docs.text:
Open your Ubuntu terminal (via Windows Terminal) and run:

# Check Git (usually pre-installed in Ubuntu)
git --version

# Check Docker
docker --version

docs.title: Ansible Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Ansible is a configuration management and automation tool.

docs.title: Basic Commands
docs.text: Command Description ansible all -m ping Ping all hosts in inventory ansible-playbook playbook.yml Run a playbook ansible-galaxy init <role> Initialize a new role

docs.title: Inventory
docs.text:
Save as hosts.ini:

[webservers]
192.168.1.10
192.168.1.11

[dbservers]
192.168.1.20

docs.title: Playbook Example
docs.text:
Save as playbook.yml:

---
- name: Install Nginx
  hosts: webservers
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Ensure Nginx is installed
      apt:
        name: nginx
        state: present
    - name: Ensure Nginx is running
      service:
        name: nginx
        state: started

docs.title: AWS CLI Cheat Sheet
docs.text: The AWS CLI allows you to manage AWS services from the command line.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
aws configure

You will be prompted for: * AWS Access Key ID * AWS Secret Access Key * Default region name (e.g., us-east-1) * Default output format (json)

docs.title: S3 (Simple Storage Service)
docs.text:
# List buckets
aws s3 ls

# Copy file to bucket
aws s3 cp myfile.txt s3://my-bucket/

# Sync directory
aws s3 sync ./local-folder s3://my-bucket/

docs.title: EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud)
docs.text:
# List instances
aws ec2 describe-instances

# Start an instance
aws ec2 start-instances --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0

# Stop an instance
aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0

docs.title: Docker Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Docker allows you to package applications into containers.

docs.title: Basic Commands
docs.text: Command Description docker run <image> Run a container from an image docker ps List running containers docker ps -a List all containers (including stopped) docker images List available images docker stop <id> Stop a running container docker rm <id> Remove a container docker rmi <image> Remove an image

docs.title: Building Images
docs.text:
Create a Dockerfile:

FROM python:3.9-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
CMD ["python", "app.py"]

Build the image:

docker build -t my-app:v1 .

docs.title: Running Containers
docs.text:
# Run in background (-d) and map port (-p host:container)
docker run -d -p 8080:80 my-app:v1

docs.title: Git Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Git is a distributed version control system.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

docs.title: Basic Commands
docs.text: Command Description git init Initialize a new repository git clone <url> Clone an existing repository git status Check the status of files git add . Stage all changes git commit -m "msg" Commit staged changes git push origin main Push changes to remote git pull Pull changes from remote

docs.title: Branching
docs.text:
# Create a new branch
git checkout -b feature-branch

# Switch to a branch
git checkout main

# Merge branch into current branch
git merge feature-branch

docs.title: Undoing Changes
docs.text:
# Discard changes in working directory
git checkout -- <file>

# Unstage a file
git reset HEAD <file>

docs.title: Jenkins Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Jenkins is an open-source automation server for CI/CD.

docs.title: Installation (Docker)
docs.text:
The easiest way to run Jenkins is via Docker:

docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 50000:50000 -v jenkins_home:/var/jenkins_home jenkins/jenkins:lts

Access it at http://localhost:8080.

docs.title: Jenkinsfile (Declarative Pipeline)
docs.text:
Create a Jenkinsfile in your repository:

pipeline {
    agent any

    stages {
        stage('Build') {
            steps {
                echo 'Building...'
                sh 'make build'
            }
        }
        stage('Test') {
            steps {
                echo 'Testing...'
                sh 'make test'
            }
        }
        stage('Deploy') {
            steps {
                echo 'Deploying...'
                sh './deploy.sh'
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Kubernetes Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Kubernetes (K8s) is a container orchestration platform.

docs.title: Basic kubectl Commands
docs.text: Command Description kubectl get pods List all pods in the namespace kubectl get svc List all services kubectl get nodes List cluster nodes kubectl apply -f <file.yaml> Create/Update resources from a file kubectl delete -f <file.yaml> Delete resources defined in a file kubectl logs <pod> View logs of a pod kubectl exec -it <pod> -- bash Open a shell inside a pod

docs.title: Simple Pod Definition
docs.text:
Save as pod.yaml:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80

Apply it:

kubectl apply -f pod.yaml

docs.title: Terraform Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Terraform is an Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool.

docs.title: Basic Commands
docs.text: Command Description terraform init Initialize the working directory terraform plan Show changes to be applied terraform apply Apply the changes terraform destroy Destroy the infrastructure terraform validate Check if configuration is valid

docs.title: Example: Create a Local File
docs.text:
Save as main.tf:

resource "local_file" "example" {
  content  = "Hello, DevOps!"
  filename = "${path.module}/hello.txt"
}

Run:

terraform init
terraform apply
